=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller's SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

**Scope:** This review is based only on the Seller's cover note, Seller Update and Disclosure Letter. I have not seen the full SPA or the underlying DD-002 to DD-012 documents. NSW counsel should verify the legal points, especially the Privacy Act, tax and consumer law points.

## Headline view

The package is built so that every known problem is disclosed, and disclosed matters are then excluded from warranty claims. Combined with the general cap, the Seller would carry almost no risk for matters it has already identified. The buyer would bear those risks while paying the full AUD 24m. The Seller's framing ("FINAL", "not intended to be re-opened", "market standard") is advocacy. Nothing is agreed until signed, and I would not accept those statements without checking Wattlebridge's own record of what was agreed at principal level.

## Key issues

**1. Known issues are being pushed onto the buyer through disclosure**
- Clause 1.1 discloses everything in the data room as at 22 September 2026. Clause 1.2 adds the statutory registers and public records. Clause 8.3 bars claims for anything the buyer "had knowledge" of, including anything "discoverable".
- Together, these would exclude the very matters the Seller has disclosed in its Disclosure Letter, leaving the buyer with no warranty recourse for them.
- The "discoverable" test is the most dangerous. Almost any issue is discoverable in a data room.
- The disclosure is also stale. It speaks at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026.

**2. Known liabilities are not priced**

Aggregating the Seller's own disclosures:

| Item | Amount | Seller's treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, not repaid | Release "following Completion" |
| Employee Completion bonuses (DD-005) | AUD 420k, plus possible payroll tax/super/on-costs | Excluded from funds flow |
| Ironquay SOW3 open fees (DD-010) | AUD 180k, no payment receipt | Indemnity limited to SOW3 fee |
| Sandbar supplier renewals | AUD 330k | "Ordinary course" |
| **Subtotal (excluding on-costs)** | **~AUD 4.13m** | |

- This is close to the entire AUD 4.8m general cap, and the Seller would argue none of it is recoverable under warranty.
- On a debt-free, cash-free basis, Riverlark debt and seller-triggered bonuses should reduce the price at Completion, not sit as post-Completion claims.
- The funds flow omits the bonuses. Read literally, the buyer funds them.

**3. General cap, basket and de minimis (Clauses 12.1 and 12.2)**
- A 20% cap (AUD 4.8m) is at the high end of what the Seller's own preamble describes as market, and it sits well below total known exposure.
- The AUD 25k de minimis and AUD 250k deductible basket are both Seller-favourable. A deductible means the buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of every claim, which is about 1% of price, plus each small claim below AUD 25k. Push for a tipping basket (once exceeded, the whole claim is recoverable) and a lower de minimis, or argue for a smaller basket given the disclosed issues.
- The Seller's "10–20% cap" and "1% basket" references are market ranges, not binding terms. Market practice for SaaS deals varies with the risk profile, and this deal has significant identified risk.

**4. Time limits (Clauses 12.3 and 13)**
- Eighteen months for general warranties is short for SaaS, where tax, data protection and IP issues often surface later.
- The Seller's proposal that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims" would cap title, fundamental and tax claims at 18 months. That is not acceptable.
- Ask for at least 24 months for general warranties, with fundamental, title and tax claims running for longer (commonly at least 6 years for title, and until the relevant ATO amendment periods expire for tax). Confirm the position under the Limitation Act 1969 (NSW) with counsel.

**5. Fundamental and title warranties (caps and time limits)**
- Capacity and title warranties should not be subject to the general cap or time limits. Their value is the full price. The Seller's "administrative simplicity" argument does not justify this.
- The Seller's title evidence is only the share register at DD-012. Require independent verification: ASIC current company extract, PPSR search over the shares, confirmation of no encumbrances, and a certified copy of the register. Title should be a fundamental warranty capped at the price.

**6. Exclusive remedy, non-reliance and "all Claims" language (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)**
- These should not apply to fraud, wilful concealment, or claims for specific indemnities.
- A non-reliance clause should not prevent claims based on fraud. Non-reliance and exclusive remedy language should also not restrict any rights the buyer has under the Australian Consumer Law or other statute that cannot be excluded. Confirm the exact position with counsel.

**7. Buyer knowledge / anti-sandbagging (Clause 8.3)**
- Reject this. A buyer should be able to claim for breach of warranty even if it knew of the breach, subject to a clear disclosure standard.
- If the Seller insists on a knowledge qualifier, limit it to actual, specific knowledge of named individuals at signing, and remove "discoverable" and "advisers" from it.
- Public registers should not be deemed disclosed. Disclosure should be specific and fairly presented, not general.

**8. Specific indemnities needed**
The Seller's Clause 11.1 indemnity for Ironquay is limited to the SOW3 payment. The buyer needs:
- **Ironquay:** a full indemnity for any IP ownership, licensing or third-party claim relating to the Ironquay development and SOW3 materials, plus the open AUD 180k. Not subject to basket or de minimis.
- **Employee bonuses:** a price deduction (or Seller-funded payment) for AUD 420k plus any payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs, whether or not conditions are met.
- **Privacy/export incident (DD-006):** a specific indemnity covering regulatory investigation, notification costs (under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme in the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), if an eligible data breach is established), forensic costs, third-party claims and remediation. The Seller says it is "not expected to be material", but it has not established whether unauthorised access occurred. Require a forensic investigation before signing, and a retention or escrow.
- **Tax:** a pre-Completion tax indemnity, uncapped up to price, not subject to the basket. The Seller's statement that tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime" is not acceptable.

**9. Conditions and completion mechanics**
- **Bluefen (Clauses 3 and 6.3):** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). The Seller's proposal to "use reasonable endeavours" and treat consent as satisfied on receipt of the counterparty's written consent is weak. Make Bluefen's written consent, with conditions satisfied, an express condition precedent. Do not allow waiver without buyer consent. Consider a price adjustment or walk right if it is not obtained by a fixed date.
- **Riverlark (Clauses 2 and 7):** The facility must be repaid from the purchase price at Completion, with a discharge of security and PPSR release delivered at or before Completion. A release "following Completion" leaves the buyer exposed to the security.
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Confirm whether landlord consent is required for a change of control. If it is, it should be a condition precedent or a specific warranty.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Confirm whether the assignment restriction is triggered by a share sale. If it is, consent should be a condition precedent.
- **Supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011):** Require a schedule of each renewal, its term, termination rights, and whether it is ordinary course. Any unavoidable commitment beyond Completion should be treated as debt-like or a price deduction.

**10. Disclosure Letter general terms**
- Clause 1.4 (no admissions) is standard, but the Seller should not use it to avoid giving specific warranties on the disclosed facts.
- Clause 11 ("The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts") shifts the burden of assessment to the buyer. It should be deleted or qualified so the Seller stands behind the accuracy of what it discloses.

## Recommendations (summary)

**Priority 1: Must-have before any further negotiation**
1. Reject "FINAL" and "not to be re-opened". Verify against Wattlebridge's principal-level record.
2. Delete the general disclosure of the data room and public records (Clauses 1.1, 1.2). Require specific disclosure.
3. Delete or narrow the buyer-knowledge clause (Clause 8.3).
4. Require a bring-down of the Disclosure Letter to signing and to Completion. The current date is past the 22 September 2026 cut-off.
5. Treat Riverlark debt (~AUD 3.2m), the AUD 420k bonuses (plus on-costs) and the AUD 180k Ironquay open fees as price adjustments at Completion, not post-Completion claims.

**Priority 2: Risk allocation**
6. Specific indemnities for Ironquay IP and open fees, the privacy/export incident, pre-Completion tax, and bonuses.
7. Fundamental and title warranties: outside the general cap, time limits of at least 6 years, capped at price.
8. Tax claims: time limit until ATO amendment periods expire, outside basket.
9. General cap: resist 20%. Push for a higher cap (or at least 20% plus specific indemnities outside the cap), and a tipping basket with a lower de minimis.
10. General warranty time limit: at least 24 months.

**Priority 3: Conditions and verification**
11. Bluefen written consent as a condition precedent, with a walk right if not delivered by a fixed date.
12. Riverlark discharge and PPSR release at Completion.
13. Confirm lease and Mossvale consent requirements, and make consent a condition where triggered.
14. Forensic investigation of the DD-006 incident before signing, with a retention or escrow if unresolved.
15. Independent title verification: ASIC extract, PPSR search, certified share register.
16. Supplier renewal schedule, with any committed beyond Completion treated as debt-like.

**Priority 4: Carve-outs**
17. Exclusive remedy, non-reliance and limitation provisions should not apply to fraud, wilful concealment, specific indemnities or non-excludable statutory rights.

If you can share the full SPA and the underlying data room documents (DD-002 to DD-012), I can check the exact wording of the Seller's clauses against these points and draft the buyer's mark-up language.
